This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail.

The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No. 114 of 2023, registered at Police Outpost Sonkyari, Police Station Sanna, District Digitally Jashpur, Chhattisgarh for the offence under Sections 363, 366-A and signed by VEDPRAKASH VEDPRAKASH DEWANGAN DEWANGAN

sentences.text: 2. The case of prosecution in brief is that, on 25.08.2023, the father of the prosecutrix lodged a missing report that his minor daughter is missing since 15.08.2023 and her whereabouts could not be traced out.
The police has registered the offence under Section 363 of IPC and started the investigation.

During the investigation, the prosecutrix was recovered on 05.02.2024 from the possession of the applicant from Himachal Pradesh and after recording her statement, the other offences of Sections 366-A, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act have been added.
The applicant has been arrested on 07.02.2024 and charge sheet has been filed.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that there is no cogent evidence with respect to Sunil Ram vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70575569/

sentences.text: the age of the prosecutrix.

She, being a major girl, having love affair with the applicant and eloped with him on her own will, both of them had gone to Himachal Pradesh and resided as husband and wife and earning their livelihood.
She has not made any complaint while traveling upto Himachal Pradesh and also while staying with the applicant there.
She would further submit that the prosecutrix has been examined before the learned trial Court as PW-1 and has not supported the prosecution's case.
The applicant is in jail since 07.02.2024 and final adjudication of the case will take some time, therefore he may be enlarged on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents annexed with the application.

6. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, considering the nature of the allegation and the material collected during the investigation, further considering that the prosecutrix has been examined before the learned trial Court and has not supported the prosecution's case.

The applicant is in jail since 07.02.2024, without commenting anything on merits, I am inclined to release him on bail.
7.
Consequently, the present application filed by the applicant for grant of regular bail is hereby allowed.

8. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court,
on following conditions:-
(i) He shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such fact to the Court.
(ii) He shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial.
(iii) He shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the concerned trial Court till disposal of the trial.
